Stabilizing non-noble metal electrocatalysts for acidic water oxidation
abstract: Renewable-powered water splitting needs to move beyond scarce iridium, but non-noble metal electrocatalysts dissolve in acid. This review maps their degradation and stabilization tactics. It also flags a neglected real-world problem: fluctuating solar and wind start-stop cycles speed decay that steady lab tests miss, which demands device-level testing for scalable clean hydrogen.

title: Through the lens of fog
High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur–sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur–carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm−2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15–25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg−1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li–In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage.

title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
The person behind the scientist
Plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots for crop disease management
abstract: Fungal plant pathogens, such as Fusarium graminearum, can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security worldwide. Fungicides play a key role in conventional plant disease management, but their overuse has led to severe environmental pollution, harm to non-target species and the emergence of resistant pathogens. To tackle these issues, sustainable alternatives are urgently needed. Here we used nanotechnology to synthesize amphiphilic carbon dots (CDs) derived from turmeric plant. Under natural-light illumination conditions, the CDs target the biomembrane system of F. graminearum via generating reactive oxygen species in situ to inactivate fungal spores and reduce pathogenicity in vitro and in planta. The CDs adhere to and enter the spores by endocytosis, localizing to membranous organelles and causing oxidative damage that disrupts cellular homeostasis. A 3-year field trial demonstrated that the CDs can efficiently control wheat Fusarium head blight with little effect on wheat growth, microorganisms and non-target organisms (earthworm, honeybee and silkworm). Overall, this research introduces an eco-friendly antifungal strategy, thus offering a sustainable solution to global challenges in food security and ecosystem health.

title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes
abstract: Developing sustainable lithium-ion battery cathode materials with high energy density and structural stability is critical for the global clean energy transition. Oxygen-redox chemistry in lithium-rich layered oxides offers additional capacity, but irreversible structural changes cause progressive voltage decay. Here we report a family of lithium-rich layered cathodes, Lix(Li0.15Ni0.20Mn0.65)O2, with a unique O6-type stacking sequence formed by atomic-scale intergrowth of O3- and O1-type subunit cells, and reveal how this architecture regulates oxygen-redox activity and structural reversibility. Combining first-principles calculations with structural and spectroscopic analyses, we show that this intergrown architecture suppresses destructive structural evolution responsible for oxygen-redox degradation, including transition-metal migration and irreversible oxygen dimerization. By preserving the local oxygen coordination environment during cycling, the O6 framework stabilizes oxygen-redox activity and mitigates the associated voltage decay. Consequently, the O6-type cathode exhibits negligible voltage decay and superior energy density retention. Our findings establish atomic-scale stacking as a key design parameter for controlling structural dynamics and oxygen-redox reversibility, providing a general strategy for developing durable, high-energy-density cathodes for next-generation green batteries.

title: SMC5/6 safeguards chromatin compartments and TAD boundaries for genome stability
abstract: SMC5/6, a member of the Structural Maintenance of Chromosomes family, coordinates 3D genome organization, chromatin states, and transcriptional regulation, yet its role in higher-order chromatin architecture remains poorly defined. Here, we investigate the impact of conditional SMC5 depletion in human B lymphoblastoid cells. Hi-C analyses reveal global rewiring of chromatin interactions, with increased long-range and reduced short-range contacts, leading to altered large-scale chromosome organization. SMC5 loss induces changes in 3D genome compartmentalization affecting ~2% of the genome and is accompanied by transcriptional upregulation of inflammatory and cancer-associated gene programs. SMC5 depletion also promotes double-strand break accumulation, preferentially in active compartments and following gene expression levels. However, regions undergoing architectural reorganization display comparatively fewer breaks, indicating that chromatin changes are not driven by DNA damage. Together, our findings establish SMC5/6 as a key regulator of chromatin compartmentalization and TAD boundary integrity, linking 3D genome organization to transcriptional control and genome stability.

title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
abstract: Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. Here, we show that rapid lateral carrier separation in these nanostructures produces observable signatures in ultrafast spectroscopy. Using combined time-resolved photoluminescence and time-resolved differential reflectance spectroscopy, we observe photoluminescence exhibiting fast decay while differential reflection remains stable. This indicates rapid carrier separation. Studies of temperature and power-dependent photoluminescence confirm that carrier separation dominates over recombination-driven decay, and Mg doping studies reveal that stronger band bending enhances the carrier separation. The physical interpretation of the observations is supported by a numerical model including drift, diffusion, and thermal relaxation. The results provide critical insights into charge carrier dynamics in InGaN nanostructures, highlighting their potential for efficient photocatalysis.

title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration
abstract: Non-degradative C–H functionalization provides a promising route to upgrade polyolefins into functional materials by installing polar groups onto the carbon backbones, but few methods are universally applicable to the diverse and mixed polyolefins commonly encountered in waste streams. Herein, we report a rapid, selective, and broadly applicable C–H nitration strategy for the direct upcycling of mixed polyolefins. Driven by the low steric hindrance and radical nature of NO2, diverse substrates are nitrated with high selectivity (87–97%), reaching functionalization degrees of up to 2.4 mol% in just 5 min while substantially maintaining their molecular weights. The functionalized polymers not only exhibit enhanced tensile and adhesion properties, but can also be formulated into a dynamic covalent polymer network that displays 23-fold higher toughness than the original polyolefin mixture. This work establishes a rapid and general C–H nitration as a scalable and waste-compatible strategy to upcycle mixed polyolefins beyond depolymerization.

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract: Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
abstract: Antireflection coatings are widely used in optical systems to increase transmission and suppress unwanted reflections by matching the optical impedance across a uniform interface. Applying the same idea to metasurfaces is fundamentally more challenging because their wavefront control relies on arrays of geometrically distinct meta-atoms, presenting as a spatially varying optical impedance. Here we show that vertical integration can overcome this limitation by allowing bilayer meta-atoms to act simultaneously as phase shifters and impedance-matching stacks. By treating meta-atoms as multilayer thin films, we derive a design rule that links the effective refractive indices of two independently patterned layers and identifies antireflective bilayer libraries with full 0–2π transmission phase coverage. We demonstrate the approach with a free-standing TiO2/TiO2 metalens operating at 1,310 nm, which suppresses reflection below that of bare glass while maintaining diffraction-limited focusing. These results establish bilayer metasurfaces as a platform for jointly engineering optical impedance and wavefront response at the meta-atom level.

title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
abstract: Linking electrode microstructure to electrochemical performance is essential for optimizing Li-ion batteries. However, this requires mechanistic four-dimensional observations at the ultimate spatiotemporal scales, which remain elusive. Here we demonstrate the use of interrupted-operando synchrotron X-ray nano-holotomography combined with digital volume correlation to track chemomechanical dynamics at both particle (local) and electrode (averaged) scales. Quantitative scale-bridging image analysis is applied to composite graphite–silicon electrodes during their electrochemical formation cycle. Our findings reveal that local ionic diffusion properties, graphite particle morphology and position in the electrode, distance to silicon clusters, surface contact with the liquid electrolyte solution, and mechanical deformations all directly affect local electrochemical activity and irreversibility, although these parameters are not equally important. In particular, we identify fast ionic diffusion channels that play a key role and counterbalance intrinsic depth-dependent reaction heterogeneities arising from ionic and electronic diffusion limitations. The various structural factors that determine the electrochemical performance of composite graphite–silicon electrodes in Li-ion batteries beyond ensemble properties are classified using a scale of influence, providing a practical framework for the optimization of materials and electrode manufacturing.

title: Sorting reaction pathways to program alkene skeletons
Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
abstract: Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented p orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, showing global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons, as revealed by 1H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

title: Influence of Local Curvature and Structural Chirality on Magnetic Spin Textures in Fe Thin‐Film Möbius Bands
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The Möbius band is a fascinating three‐dimensional (3D) architecture that exhibits a geometric chirality where left‐ and right‐handed twists cannot be interchanged via continuous rotation, along with a varying extrinsic curvature. Here, we demonstrate that spin textures in arrays of Fe magnetic Möbius structures are fundamentally governed by their geometric chirality and extrinsic curvature. Magnetic full‐field soft x‐ray transmission microscopy reveals that the unique geometry drives domain fragmentation into nontrivial arrangements in regions of maximal curvature, along with the formation of nontrivial vortex domains. Magnetometry and first‐order reversal curve measurements reveal a complex magnetization reversal process, as the lateral and vertical portions of the Möbius structures respond differently to in‐plane and out‐of‐plane applied fields. Micromagnetic simulations confirm a vortex state with geometry‐driven preferred circulation direction. The resulting spin textures propagate either clockwise or counterclockwise along the Möbius structures, depending on the direction of an in‐plane magnetic field applied along the primary bend of the structure. These geometric‐chirality‐driven effects are manifested in the experimentally captured evolution of the remanent magnetization. Our results demonstrate a new platform where curvature and real space topology of 3D nanostructures may be used as degrees of freedom to tailor spin textures.

title: Synergistic Integration of Materials and Design Strategies for Next‐Generation Stretchable Displays
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Stretchable displays rely on sophisticated integration enabled by materials engineering, structural strategies, and micro‐nano integration, encompassing stretchable substrates, conducting and semiconducting components. This review provides a focused discussion of recent technological advances. We highlight key innovations in stretchable electrodes, interconnects, emissive materials, transistor arrays, circuit layouts, and deformable substrates for their roles in improving electrical uniformity, mechanical resilience, and display performance. Additionally, we summarize the latest strategies for achieving stretchability, either by using intrinsically elastic electronic materials or by structurally engineering rigid components. We introduce emerging applications with substantial potential, including epidermal human‐machine interfaces, conformal biomedical monitoring and visualization, soft robotics with distributed optical feedback, and skin‐integrated augmented reality (AR)/virtual reality (VR) systems, to illustrate the transformative opportunities ahead for stretchable display technologies.

title: Electronic Spin States in Oxygen Reduction: From Identification Divergence to Mechanism Clarification
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a cornerstone process in clean‐energy technologies including fuel cells, metal–air batteries, and electrochemical hydrogen peroxide synthesis. Emerging evidence has established the electronic spin states of transition‐metal active centers as a critical descriptor that governs ORR activity and selectivity, yet present studies of the same metal center have reported divergent electronic spin states and ORR pathway selectivity. This review attempts to perform a comprehensive discussion about this divergence. The fundamentals of spin states are first introduced within the frameworks of crystal field theory and molecular orbital theory and the principal characterization techniques for spin states identification. Subsequently, the contradictory correlations between spin states and ORR selectivity reported in different catalytic systems are critically analyzed in terms of
                    d
                    ‐orbital occupancy and reaction kinetics. Furthermore, rationally regulating spin states strategies are elucidated to optimize ORR performance. Finally, key challenges and future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the need for in situ characterization, advanced theoretical modeling, and unambiguous identification of active sites. This review will furnish theoretical guidance for subsequent investigations of spin effects, and provide insights into extending spin state engineering to other small‐molecule electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Strong and Thermally Conductive Graphene‐Bamboo Nanocomposites by Topological Fiber‐Network Engineering Towards Intelligent Energy‐Efficient Floors
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Smart floor‐heating systems that integrate occupancy sensing with localized thermal regulation offer a promising route toward low‐carbon buildings, yet existing flooring materials cannot simultaneously provide robust mechanical properties and rapid heat delivery. Here, a topological fiber‐network engineering and thermorheology‐assisted assembly strategy is reported that enables continuous thermal‐transport and load‐bearing networks to coexist within a single material. Long bamboo fibers form a topologically entangled framework that simultaneously serves as a mechanically robust scaffold and a three‐dimensional template for graphene nanoplatelet assembly, while thermorheological phenol‐formaldehyde (PF) resin facilitates their rearrangement into ordered face‐to‐face configurations under low pressure. The resulting graphene–bamboo composites (GBC) exhibit metal‐level thermal conductivities of 12.8–116.7 W m
                    −
                    1
                    K
                    −
                    1
                    together with outstanding flexural strengths of 75–155 MPa, outperforming conventional flooring materials. When integrated into a pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating system, the composites enable rapid thermal homogenization and occupant‐responsive localized heating. Whole‐building simulations indicate that nationwide adoption of the composite in pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating systems in China could reduce annual heating‐electricity consumption by up to ∼208 TWh, corresponding to a ∼37% reduction compared with conventional wood flooring. This work establishes the integration of topological fiber‐network engineering with thermorheology‐assisted assembly as a general strategy for overcoming the thermal–mechanical trade‐off in structural biomass composites and advancing energy‐efficient building materials.

title: Trace‐Metal‐Assisted Flash Synthesis for Fast‐Charging Graphite Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Graphite has remained the dominant anode material in lithium–ion batteries (LIBs), powering portable electronics and electric vehicles (EVs). However, sluggish Li
                    +
                    diffusion kinetics in natural and synthetic graphite can severely limit charging rates. Overcoming this bottleneck requires the rational design of graphite architectures that enable rapid Li
                    +
                    transport in LIBs. Here, we disclose a trace‐metal‐assisted flash (TMF) process for the millisecond synthesis of catalytic flashed graphite (CFGr) with exceptionally fast‐charging capabilities. The TMF process induces in situ formation of trace nickel nanoclusters that catalyze ultrafast graphitization of amorphous carbon into highly ordered graphite within <1 s. Raman spectroscopy shows an exceedingly clean graphite material with
                    I
                    D
                    /
                    I
                    G
                    of 0.09, with calculations yielding an interlayer bonding energy (
                    E
                    b
                    ) of −2.297 eV, while diffraction reveals an interlayer spacing (d
                    002
                    ) of 3.4 Å. These features enhance structural stability and Li
                    +
                    accessibility. Consequently, optimized CFGr achieves a high reversible capacity of 347.4 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.25 C and retains 158.8 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 15 C with 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles, outperforming the rate and cyclability of both commercial graphite and graphite prepared by flash Joule heating. The TMF route can replace conventional energy‐intensive graphitization, reducing energy use and emissions by over 80% and lowering the production cost of premium fast‐charging synthetic graphite by ∼80% to only US$0.84 kg
                    −1
                    . These findings establish a promising pathway to advance fast‐charging graphite anodes into next‐generation LIBs.

title: Bioinspired Molecular‐Scale Tape Interface Towards Ultrahigh‐Pixel‐Density Flexible Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Devices
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Flexible, high‐density integrated optoelectronics underpin emerging wearable information systems and human–machine interfaces. However, as pixel size decreases to a few micrometers, emission uniformity and performance of flexible light emitting diodes (LED) degrade severely due to microscale electrical and optical nonuniformity of electrodes especially after bending, hindering their potential applications. Inspired by fish scales, we propose a molecular‐scale tape interface as a transparent electrode for ultrahigh‐pixel‐density flexible LEDs. An atomically thin MXene layer, assembled via liquid–air interfacial assembly, conformally adheres to indium tin oxide through reversible hydrogen bonding and van der Waals coupling, enabling stress redistribution, crack bridging, and potential homogenization. This electrode enables flexible quantum‐dot LEDs with uniform micro‐area current and emission up to 25 400 ppi and a record external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.4%, maintaining performance after 3000 bending cycles. This biomimetic transparent‐electrode interfacial strategy unites mechanical flexibility with ultrahigh pixel density, advancing high‐density integrated optoelectronic architectures.

title: Molecular Engineering of Redox Mediator for Accelerated Multi‐Electron Transfer Reactions in Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lithium–sulfur and lithium–oxygen batteries are highly attractive due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy densities, while their performance is severely constrained by sluggish multiphase reaction rates and limited reaction stability at the cathodes. The conventional solid‐phase catalysts suffer from small interfacial contact area and activity loss of active sites, while the mobile redox mediators (RMs) present a new paradigm for accelerating multi‐electron transfer pathways through a solution‐mediated electron transfer pathway. This review first discusses the critical rate‐limiting factors governing reaction rate at the cathode, and then systematically examines the latest advances in the molecular engineering of RMs for cathode catalysis from the viewpoint of redox potential, solubility, molecular size, and chemical stability. Following these points, we comprehensively analyze, from both thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, how the molecular engineering of RMs affects the redox potential, solubility, stability, and so on. These characteristics strongly dictate the specific capacity and lifespan, elucidating key structure–activity relationships. Finally, we propose systemic strategies expanding beyond isolated liquid‐phase catalysis toward solid–liquid synergistic design and functionalized electrolyte/separator engineering.

title: Advances and Perspectives of Cobalt‐Free Li‐Rich Mn‐Based Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxides (LRMOs) are prioritized for next‐generation batteries due to their high theoretical specific capacity and energy density. In particular, the cobalt‐free LRMOs offer additional competitive advantages due to their lowered production cost and reduced resource dependence. However, the cobalt‐free LRMOs still suffer from persistent structural stability challenges, exhibiting low initial Coulombic efficiency, rapid capacity and voltage decay, and inferior rate capability. To advance cobalt‐free LRMO development, massive research efforts focused on effective regulation strategies have emerged recently. It is therefore imperative to timely summarize these recent works to systematically evaluate the attained achievements, recognize the unresolved issues, and formulate the key optimization approaches in the next stage; however, such related reviews for cobalt‐free LRMOs remain limited. Herein, we carefully examine the fundamental advances in cobalt‐free LRMOs and give a comprehensive review work. Initially, the microstructure of cobalt‐free LRMOs is dissected, and the corresponding electrochemical mechanism is elucidated. In addition, the faced challenges are described and analyzed in detail. More importantly, the currently proposed modification strategies are primarily discussed from the microstructure regulation, element doping and surface coating views. Finally, the significant perspectives are highlighted.

title: Re‐Evaluating the Role of Water in Hexacyanoferrate Cathodes for Sodium and Potassium Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hexacyanoferrates (HCFs) are among the most promising cathode materials for sodium‐ion and potassium‐ion batteries owing to their open three‐dimensional framework, high operating voltage, and fast alkali‐ion transport. As an unavoidable constituent of hexacyanoferrates (HCFs), water is intimately associated with crystal growth, vacancy formation, local coordination, and framework stability. Water has long been regarded primarily as a detrimental impurity in cathodes because it blocks ion transport, accelerates electrolyte decomposition, and promotes structural degradation. However, recent studies indicate that interstitial and coordinated water exhibit distinct binding strengths, mobilities, and electrochemical reactivities, rendering their roles far more complex than can be described by total water content alone. In this Review, we re‐evaluate the role of water in HCF cathodes by redefining it from a structural impurity to a functional component. We discuss how water governs crystal structure, electronic structure, ion transport, interfacial reactions, and electrochemical performance. We further summarize advanced characterization techniques, particularly neutron methods, for probing the dynamic behavior of water molecules, and highlight regulation strategies. This work establishes a unified framework linking water with crystal, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior, providing guidance for the rational design of high‐performance HCF cathodes.

title: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) binds talin and is anchored at the postsynaptic density by direct PDZ interactions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) is a serine/threonine kinase essential for brain development and function. Mutations in
                    CDKL5
                    cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy associated with impaired synapse formation and function. However, how CDKL5 mutations disrupt synaptic function remains unclear. Here, we show that the major neuronal isoform of CDKL5 contains a C-terminal PDZ domain–binding motif that mediates direct binding to PSD-95 and SHANK PDZ domains and recruits CDKL5 to the postsynaptic density. Disrupting this motif mislocalized CDKL5, reduced dendritic spine density, and impaired spine maturation. We also show that the CDKL5 kinase domain binds the R8 rod domain of the mechanosensitive scaffold talin. Mutation of the talin-binding interface or reduced cellular contractility altered CDKL5 positioning relative to focal adhesions. These findings define how CDKL5 is targeted to synapses, suggest that talin mechanoswitching may position CDKL5 kinase activity, and highlight the importance of C-terminal anchoring for interpreting pathogenic truncations.

title: SeqA-mediated sister loci cohesion regulates the efficiency and fidelity of DNA double-strand break repair across the E. coli genome
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
In
                    Escherichia coli
                    , SeqA-mediated cohesion at snap loci on the right replichore persists longer, but its role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair remains untested. Here, we show that site-specific DSBs at snap loci confer higher cell survival than nonsnap loci. With perturbations affecting sister cohesion [Δ
                    seqA
                    , topoisomerase IV overexpression (T4-OE)], this survival advantage was progressively reduced, with the combined Δ
                    seqA
                    T4-OE strain retaining only a transient advantage. The increased survival correlates with faster repair, reflected by rapid restoration of locus copy number and shorter-lived, thinner RecA–green fluorescent protein filaments. Consistent with more accurate repair, snap loci exhibited lower mutation accumulation under normal and antibiotic stress conditions. Comparative genome analysis of
                    E. coli
                    strains revealed higher GATC motif counts and higher sequence conservation. Together, these findings suggest that the chromosomal organization associated with prolonged sister cohesion at snap loci promotes efficient homologous recombination–mediated DSB repair and contributes to genome conservation.

title: Light-guided photophosphorylation nanorobot rescues injured cardiomyocytes via in situ bioenergetic restoration
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Myocardial injury is a leading cause of death worldwide and is accompanied by profound mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction in impaired cardiomyocytes. Restoring cellular bioenergetic homeostasis could be a promising strategy to promote cardiac repair; however, current clinical adenosine triphosphate (ATP) injection therapies yield limited efficacy due to the inability to achieve in situ, targeted delivery. Here, we develop a photoactivated phosphorylation nanorobot engineered to rescue impaired metabolism via targeted, in situ ATP synthesis within cardiomyocytes. These Janus photophosphorylation nanorobots are fabricated through mechanical extrusion–assisted phase separation, enabling the asymmetric integration of chromatophore-coupled F
                    o
                    F
                    l
                    -ATPases. Under structured near-infrared irradiation, the nanorobots exhibit synergistic F
                    o
                    F
                    l
                    -ATPase rotation, which simultaneously drives active propulsion and high-yield ATP catalysis. Following targeted internalization and efficient lysosomal escape, the nanorobots achieve deep penetration into injured myocardial tissue. Intracellularly, the localized elevation of ATP rebalances the NAD
                    +
                    /NADH ratio, suppresses pathological mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, and mitigates calcium ion overload—collectively restoring mitochondrial integrity and promoting functional myocardial recovery. This self-propelled, bioenergy-restoring nanoplatform represents a rationally designed strategy for targeted therapy of energy-deficient cardiomyopathies.

title: Solubility-driven morphological decoupling enables elastic electron-deficient semiconducting polymers for fully stretchable electronics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The development of fully stretchable electronics is limited by the scarcity of electron-deficient polymers that combine high electron mobility with mechanical elasticity. Here, we report a solubility-driven morphological decoupling strategy that mitigates this trade-off by incorporating ∼10% planar, insoluble PyF units into a semicrystalline PySe backbone. This approach yields a hierarchical morphology characterized by suppressed long-range crystallinity alongside robust local aggregation. Driven by strong fluorine (F)-sulfur (S) interactions, highly ordered face-on domains function as robust physical anchors, providing the polymer network with exceptional elasticity to reversibly dissipate stress and preserve charge percolation pathways. Consequently, the resulting terpolymer largely relieves the long-standing trade-off between charge transport and mechanical stretchability, delivering a near-unity initial electron mobility (∼1.0 square centimeter per volt per second) and retaining 0.5 square centimeters per volt per second even under 100% applied strain, representing the highest performance reported to date. To demonstrate the practical utility of this system, we fabricated stretchable ambipolar inverters and phototransistors that maintain high performance under severe deformation. Notably, the phototransistors sustain an exceptional responsivity of 15.8 amperes per watt and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 2900% at 100% strain. These results establish a powerful blueprint for intrinsically elastic semiconductors, enabling the realization of high-performance, fully deformable optoelectronic systems.

title: Asymmetric interactions and feast-famine cycles drive chaos in microbial populations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Predicting the dynamics of ecological systems is a central challenge in biology. One factor that may limit predictability is ecological chaos. Theory has long suggested that even simple interactions can produce chaos, yet empirical demonstrations in living systems remain scarce. In a two-strain system of
                    Escherichia coli
                    , increasing the duration between resource replenishment reveals transitions from competitive exclusion to chaos, driven by asymmetric ecological interactions and periodic environmental forcing. Guided by these observations, we developed a dynamical systems framework grounded in empirical data that recapitulate the observed dynamics and predicts intermediate ecological states and transitions. Experimental validation of these predictions by implementing the corresponding conditions successfully reproduces the full range of predicted dynamical regimes. Because feast-famine cycles and asymmetric interactions are widespread in nature, our findings provide a model for uncovering the ecological and evolutionary significance of chaos, opening avenues to use resource fluctuation and interaction strength to quantify, monitor, and manipulate complex ecosystem behavior previously interpreted as stochasticity.

title: Denoised vibrometry reveals noncanonical filtering at the apex of the cochlea
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: How do mammals distinguish sounds with different pitch? Prevailing theory states that each position along the cochlear spiral responds best to one single stimulus frequency, forming a frequency-to-place (tonotopic) map that is preserved throughout the auditory pathways. Whether this holds in the low-frequency cochlear apex, a region important for vocal communication but technically challenging to study, is unknown. Using a differential noise-canceling technique, we recorded sound-evoked motion near the lower limit of hearing. Apical locations often had two best frequencies, contradicting the assumption of one-to-one frequency-to-place mapping. Spatially distant regions responded similarly, and brief sounds evoked synchronized motion across large distances, revealing an unusual energy propagation mode. Morphology and mathematical analyses corroborate these findings, showing that tonotopy breaks down at the apex of the cochlea. These results have important implications for cochlear implants, which currently assume tonotopic organization throughout the cochlea.

title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis CpsA interferes with the TBK1-p62 axis to inhibit xenophagy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    (Mtb) survives in macrophages by interfering with host lysosomal trafficking. Previously, we demonstrated that the Mtb protein, CpsA, is critical for bacterial survival in macrophages and infection in mice and that it can inhibit a noncanonical autophagy pathway. We also found that CpsA can interact with NDP52 and TAX1BP1, selective autophagy receptors that recognize cytosolic bacteria and target them for degradation, raising the possibility that CpsA also disrupts canonical autophagy. Here, we show that CpsA binds NDP52 and TAX1BP1 in their SKICH domains, which normally recruit the autophagy initiation machinery and TBK1. We demonstrate that CpsA prevents phagosomal recruitment of FIP200, a component of the autophagy initiation machinery, and blocks TBK1-dependent phosphorylation of p62, leading to impaired xenophagy. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how Mtb subverts host defenses, revealing that in addition to blocking noncanonical autophagy, CpsA inhibits the TBK1-p62 axis to block xenophagy.

title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10
                    8
                    and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10
                    −12
                    watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

title: Predictive model for nanoparticle incorporation into crystals reveals essential role of interfacial solution structure
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Control of interfacial phenomena remains limited by incomplete understanding of molecular-scale solution structure at solid-liquid interfaces. We address this challenge by developing and validating a comprehensive analytical model for nanoparticle incorporation during crystallization. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) probes surface functionalized to be “particle proxies” combined with three-dimensional AFM and force spectroscopy, we measure nanoparticle-calcite crystal binding energies and kinetic barriers associated with interfacial hydration layers. These measurements, together with diffusivities, parameterize a predictive model that is corroborated using surface-functionalized fluorescent silica nanoparticles incorporated into calcite. We show that surface chemistry governs incorporation by reshaping the energy landscape, with amine groups particularly favoring incorporation. Applying this approach to nanoparticles with different topologies further supports our finding that kinetic barriers play a pivotal role in incorporation processes. This synthesis science framework links interfacial solution structure, particle dynamics, and crystallization kinetics, identifying kinetic barriers as a key design principle for engineering bioinspired nanocomposites beyond empirical approaches.

title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

title: Anisotropic field suppression of charge order reveals orbital-selective Kondo hybridization in UTe2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
UTe
                    2
                    is a rare correlated quantum material where unconventional density-wave orders, Kondo physics, spin-triplet pairing, and reentrant superconductivity coexist. Because superconductivity emerges from a strongly correlated normal state, identifying and controlling intertwined normal-state orders are essential for understanding the electronic landscape where superconductivity arises. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy in a vector magnetic field, we uncover a staggered charge density wave (CDW) in high-quality UTe
                    2
                    crystals. This CDW exhibits a strong directional field response: It is completely quenched by a modest 1.7-tesla magnetic field along the quasi–one-dimensional uranium-chain direction while remaining robust against fields along other crystallographic axes. This anisotropy suggests an orbital-driven field-tuned quantum phase transition. Unexpectedly, the same field orientation concurrently suppresses the 5f Kondo resonance. Modeling indicates a switch in the dominant hybridization channel from Te 5
                    p-
                    U 5
                    f
                    to U 6
                    d-
                    U 5
                    f
                    coupling, suggesting an intimate interplay between CDW and the Kondo effect.

title: SMAD4 loss drives cancer chromosomal instability through transcription-replication conflict–associated replication stress
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cancer chromosomal instability (CIN) drives tumor evolution through generating structural and numerical chromosome aberrations. However, its molecular determinants remain poorly characterized. Here, we uncover a yet unrecognized role for the tumor suppressor
                    SMAD4
                    as a key regulator of chromosomal stability. Mechanistically, loss of
                    SMAD4
                    causes replication stress by promoting transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) and induces subsequent mitotic errors, leading to the concomitant emergence of structural and numerical CIN. While the tumor suppressor function of
                    SMAD4
                    has been predominantly attributed to transforming growth factor–β signaling, we find that its role in genome maintenance operates via bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and its transcriptional target gene
                    ID3
                    . Consequently, inhibition of BMP signaling mimics the loss of
                    SMAD4
                    , while reexpression of
                    SMAD4
                    or
                    ID3
                    in
                    SMAD4
                    -deficient colorectal or pancreatic cancer cells suppresses TRCs, replication stress, and mitotic errors. Our findings reveal a TRC- and replication stress–driven mechanism by which loss of BMP-SMAD4 signaling causes cancer CIN.

title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine–glycine–one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

title: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed drug delivery, enabling the stabilization and efficient intracellular delivery of nucleic acids. Current LNP platforms, including those used in clinical COVID-19 vaccines, rely on polyethylene glycol (PEG) to stabilize the nanoparticle. However, anti-PEG antibodies are ubiquitous in the population and are a major cause of anaphylaxis and reduced therapeutic efficacy by accelerating the blood clearance of PEGylated products. Here, we report the development of poly(2-oxazoline) (POx) lipids as alternatives. POx polymers are poorly immunogenic and mitigate accelerated blood clearance. Upon varying polymer hydrophilicity and molecular weight, we screened transfection efficiency in multiple cell lines and evaluated top candidates in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that POx-lipids incorporating short hydrophilic oxazoline chains enhance target transfection while mitigating liver expression. These POx-lipids boost expression in key extrahepatic tissues, including lymph nodes and spleen. This marks a notable advancement toward replacing PEG in LNP therapies and provides a clear path to optimizing POx-lipids for targeted vaccine and therapeutic applications.

title: LONP-1 deficiency causes dysregulated protein synthesis within mitochondria that is suppressed by mitoribosomal mutations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Mitochondrial homeostasis is maintained by molecular chaperones and proteases located within the organelle. The mitochondrial matrix-localized protease LONP-1 degrades oxidatively damaged or misfolded proteins. Importantly, LONP-1 also regulates mitochondrial DNA replication. Here, we show that mutations in
                    C. elegans
                    that impair LONP-1 function cause dysregulation of mitochondrial DNA replication, mitochondrial RNA transcription and protein synthesis within the mitochondrial matrix. LONP-1 deficient worms had reduced levels of oxidative phosphorylation proteins despite increased mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis. Via a forward genetic screen, we identified three mutations that restored mitochondrial function and the rate of development in
                    lonp-1
                    mutants to levels comparable to those in wildtype worms. Interestingly, all three suppressor mutations were found in genes encoding mitochondrial ribosome proteins. A point mutation in the mitochondrial ribosome protein MRPS-38 restored oxidative phosphorylation in
                    lonp-1
                    mutant worms. Combined, our results suggest that LONP-1 regulates mitochondrial translation and that suppressor mutations within
                    mrps-38
                    or
                    mrps-15
                    can enhance oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly when LONP-1 function is diminished.

title: Clearance of erythrocytes after subarachnoid hemorrhage: Cranial lymphatic and dural pathways
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The clearance of toxic blood products from the brain after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is critical for neurological recovery, yet the precise anatomical pathways and cellular mechanisms responsible for this process remain poorly defined. Using murine models of both arterial perforation and low-rate intracisternal injection, we have mapped a comprehensive, multifaceted network of red blood cell (RBC) distribution and clearance. We found that, while RBCs accessed peripheral lymphatic vessels via cranial nerves, an extensive distribution of extravasated erythrocytes could also be observed sequestered within nonendothelial, collagen-lined interstitial channels flanking the major dural venous sinuses. By day 2 post-SAH, regional macrophages actively cleared some trapped erythrocytes. These findings provide a detailed spatiotemporal framework of SAH blood clearance, revealing promising anatomical and cellular targets to accelerate stroke recovery.

title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency shift to realize nonlinear activation. Using Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, we uncover a transient neuron response with tunable fading memory: A 25% change in pump power results in a three-order-of-magnitude tuning in memory time, which we harness, demonstrating temporal integration of up to 50 magnon pulses. Last, we realize neuron triggering in a cascade of three neurons, highlighting its potential for connected magnonic circuits.

title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

title: Roseburia intestinalis counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut
                    Roseburia intestinalis
                    abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E
                    −/−
                    (
                    ApoE
                    
                      −/−
                    
                    ) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element–binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain–containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral
                    R. intestinalis
                    supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.

title: Enzymatic degradation of a polyester-based thermoset composite resin by an engineered cutinase from Fusarium solani
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Thermoset composites have become indispensable high-performance materials across key industrial sectors. However, existing recycling methods have yet to deliver sustainable end-of-life solutions for these materials. Here, we report the engineering of a highly active and stable biocatalyst capable of depolymerizing polyester-based thermoset composites. First, a second-generation polyester resin was designed to enhance susceptibility to enzymatic attack. Cutinase from
                    Fusarium solani
                    was selected and subsequently engineered through a combination of directed evolution and computational design using two soluble surrogate motifs representative of the redesigned resin structure. The resulting variant, which incorporated 19 mutations, exhibited a 22-fold increase in activity and an 11°C improvement in melting temperature while achieving recombinant production titers at the gram-per-liter scale in yeast cultivated in fed-batch bioreactor. This engineered enzyme depolymerized the polyester resin with a total release of 6 mM (∼1.08 grams per liter) monomethyl phthalate. Together, to our knowledge, these findings constitute the first documented example of enzymatic degradation of a complex polyester resin from thermoset composite materials.

title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) imprint gravitational signatures on the matter within their sphere of influence (SoI). Nuclear gas dynamics can hence be used to accurately measure the mass of an SMBH, yet these measurements remain elusive in the early universe. We report the first dynamical measurement of an SMBH mass at
                    z
                     > 2, based on high–spatial resolution observations of the ionized-carbon 157.7-micrometer and carbon monoxide (12-11) 216.93-micrometer emission lines that resolve the SoI in an obscured quasar at
                    z
                     = 4.6. The radial profile of the velocity dispersion reveals a clear Keplerian rise, requiring the presence of an ∼6 × 10
                    9
                    –solar mass SMBH. We propose that heavily obscured quasars allow such tracers to survive in the inner regions and may be ideal targets for increasing dynamical SMBH mass estimates in the early universe.

title: Deep ultraviolet bound states in the continuum
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Light confinement is a key strategy for enhancing light-matter interaction, and photonic crystal (PhC) slabs have emerged as a promising resonant platform due to their high
                    Q
                    factors and design flexibility. However, realizing high-
                    Q
                    PhC slabs in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) regime has remained highly challenging due to the lack of suitable materials and limitations in fabrication. In this work, we propose an etchless fabrication strategy based on electron-beam lithography and atomic layer deposition. We demonstrate a shell-type PhC slab in which a low-index photoresist core is conformally encapsulated by a high-index zirconium dioxide shell. Through angle-resolved transmittance measurements, we experimentally observe symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum in the DUV regime and achieve the highest reported
                    Q
                    factor among resonant modes in this spectral range. Furthermore, by comparing conventional bulk-type and shell-type PhC slabs in far-field response, we show that the shell-type structure maintains comparable performance while offering fabrication advantages. These results provide a practical route for realizing high-
                    Q
                    PhC slabs in the DUV and open opportunities for DUV-based molecular sensing and enhanced light-matter interaction applications.

title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Successful malaria transmission by
                    Anopheles
                    mosquitoes depends on
                    Plasmodium
                    development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that
                    Anopheles gambiae
                    SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

title: Evolution of MEIS transcription factor activity during metazoan neural development—born to be wild
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Meis TALE-class proteins pattern vertebrate neural tissue, inducing hindbrain and neural crest in
                    Xenopus laevis
                    embryos. Meis orthologs have two conserved regions: (i) Meis-specific domain and (ii) Meis-specific TALE homeodomain. Meis homeodomain proteins are present in “ancient” metazoans-eucaryotes like cnidarians, placozoans, and protozoans. We asked: When during metazoan evolution did Meis proteins acquire functionality to induce neural pattern? Using structure-function analysis in
                    Xenopus
                    , we show that the Meis-specific and Meis homeodomains suffice to induce the spinal cord but not the hindbrain. Meis proteins share a functionally conserved carboxyl-terminal transcription activation domain inducing the hindbrain. Ancient Meis proteins from
                    Trichoplax
                    and chlorophyte algae have a conserved Meis homeodomain, but lack the Meis-specific domain. Unexpectedly, these ancestral proteins robustly induce hindbrain and neural crest in
                    Xenopus
                    , unlike metazoan proteins requiring the Meis-specific domain. Thus, in early eukaryotes, Meis prototypes were “born to be wild,” having the intrinsic capacity to induce vertebrate structures like hindbrain and neural crest, despite predating them.

title: Self-assembly of bacterial volumetric patterns directed by a synthetic reaction-diffusion circuit
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Reaction-diffusion (RD) has long been proposed as a mechanism underlying biological pattern formation. However, quantitative frameworks linking circuit design to spatial organization remain limited. Here, we engineered a synthetic gene circuit, MINPAC, that couples gene expression regulation (reaction) with bacterial colony expansion and quorum sensing (diffusion) to guide bacterial cells to self-organize into periodic volumetric patterns across multiple scales, from single cells to three-dimensional colonies. The patterns exhibit robustness against environmental variations and size-dependent complexity. Mathematical modeling supports a clock-and-wavefront mechanism, where oscillatory gene expression interacts with outward expanding diffusions to generate these periodic spatial structures. Topological analysis reveals that specific network architecture is essential for pattern formation. Guided by model predictions, we further show that pattern complexity can be systematically tuned by gene dosage, with lower expression levels favoring multiple rings through faster dynamics. This work establishes a framework uniting circuit engineering and mathematical analysis for programming multicellular self-organization through RD mechanisms, with potential applications in regenerative medicine and biomaterials.

title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 (
                    n
                     = 290), anti–CTLA-4 (
                    n
                     = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 (
                    n
                     = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.
