title: Sequential anion chemistry enables dynamic interphase regulation in high-voltage LiCoO2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Lithium-ion batteries using LiCoO
                    2
                    cathodes have powered portable electronics for decades, yet their operation above 4.5 volts remains severely constrained by the unstable evolution of the cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI). Under high-voltage conditions, lattice oxygen release and continuous electrolyte oxidation progressively degrade interfacial integrity. Here, we report a diluent-mediated local solvation regulation strategy to decrease dissociative solvent molecules and induce dual anion selective redistribution around Li
                    +
                    , forming a sequential solvation motif that drives sequential anion interfacial chemistry. DFOB
                    −
                    preferentially decomposes to establish a robust initial CEI framework, while BF
                    4
                    −
                    continuously drives interfacial reactions to dynamically repair CEI defects and quench reactive oxygen species generated from lattice oxygen release. This dynamic regulation mechanism effectively stabilizes LiCoO
                    2
                    under aggressive high-voltage cycling. Consequently, the LiCoO
                    2
                    cathode delivers stable performance for 500 cycles at 4.5 volts with 73.5% capacity retention even in a low-concentration ether-based electrolyte. Furthermore, graphite||LiCoO
                    2
                    pouch cell achieves an energy density of 265.8 watt-hours per kilogram and exhibits favorable low-temperature resilience, retaining 99.1% capacity after 700 cycles at −20°C. These findings provide critical mechanistic insights into how solvation structure–driven anion chemistry can govern interfacial stability and unlock high-voltage, extreme-condition lithium-ion batteries.

title: DFT-assisted natural abundance 13C zero-field NMR via optical magnetometry
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Zero-field (ZF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy probes nuclear J-couplings without homogeneous magnetic fields, enabling inexpensive and geometrically flexible detection, including through metal. However, its broader use for chemical analysis has been limited by sensitivity and the difficulty of predicting the dense ZF multiplets. Here we demonstrate natural-abundance (1.1%) carbon-13 (
                    13
                    C) ZF spectroscopy on off-the-shelf liquids using a compact commercial rubidium-87 magnetometer without hyperpolarization or special preparation. Instrumental advances yield improved sensitivity, ≤250-millihertz linewidths, and >week-long stability, enabling isotopomer-resolved fingerprint spectra across a 13-molecule library, including rare (0.0121%) doubly
                    13
                    C-labeled species. In parallel, we demonstrate vibrationally corrected density functional theory (DFT) prediction of ZF spectra with good qualitative agreement. Comparing experiment with these calculations renders residual deviations as chemically informative, reporting on hydrogen bonding and ion pairing at high ionic strength. These results contribute toward DFT-assisted ZF NMR as a general platform for field constraint–free molecular identification and for extracting transient solution-state structure from responsive J-coupling observables.

title: A supergene converts queen-destined larvae into a novel caste in ants
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Novel morphological castes are a major source of phenotypic diversity in ants, but their genetic and developmental origins remain unresolved. Here we identify
                    ergatoid
                    , a 6.5-megabase dominant supergene that is necessary and sufficient to generate a novel caste in an undescribed species of moss ant,
                    Leptothorax AF-erg
                    . The resulting wingless (ergatoid) queens represent a distinct morphological population intermediate between workers and the ancestral winged queen caste. Morphometric and genotyping analyses show that
                    ergatoid
                    produces this caste by modifying queen-destined larvae rather than altering worker development or generating a new larval population. Transcriptomic and candidate gene analyses most strongly support altered ecdysone signaling and reduced insulin signaling as the developmental basis for this phenotype. These results show that a single large-effect genetic element can generate a novel caste by modifying a specific preexisting larval population, providing a molecular genetic explanation for how novel phenotypes can arise, more broadly, through modification of ancestral developmental plasticity.

title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA
                    CL
                    /Pt
                    CL
                    ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA
                    CL
                    /Pt
                    CL
                    range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.

title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)–responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

title: Psychedelics shift decision strategies and reconfigure orbitofrontal dynamics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Psychedelics such as psilocybin and ketamine are attracting renewed attention as rapid-acting therapeutics, yet how they reshape cognitive computations remains poorly understood. To address this, we trained mice on a free-response perceptual decision-making task that disentangles bias-driven from sensory-guided strategies. Acute administration of psilocybin or ketamine slowed decision times while improving accuracy. Behavioral modeling combining drift diffusion and GLM-HMM approaches revealed that these effects were driven by increased decision thresholds and a shift toward sensory-engaged states. Whole-brain c-Fos mapping identified modulation of distributed task-related networks, including the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). Calcium imaging showed that OFC population dynamics were reorganized under psychedelic conditions, with preserved task selectivity but altered temporal structure and shifted population correlations. Together, these findings indicate that psychedelics shift decision-making toward greater reliance on sensory evidence while reshaping cortical population dynamics, providing a system-level account of their effects on perceptual decisions.

title: The importance of organics in hydrothermal environments: A synchrotron laboratory study
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The icy moon Enceladus has hydrothermal plumes that are of astrobiologic interest as they could provide conditions to sustain life or allow for its origin. To understand the geology of hydrothermal environments on icy moons, a carbonaceous asteroid simulant similar to the material Enceladus may have accreted from was subjected to conditions analogous to that of its seafloor. The sample environment used allowed high-resolution in situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction data to be collected during the experiment. Mineral reactions were observed as they occurred. Multiple mineral reactions had a large dependence on organic matter. Organics catalyzed the breakdown of aluminosilicates and dissolved pyrite. Melanophlogite and pyrrhotite were also formed as a result of organics being present. This study reveals that organics can have a large impact on mineral reactions and likely play an important role in the geology of hydrothermal vents on icy moons, which have an abundance of organics.

title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ capable of autonomous motion monitoring and health state awareness. We develop an interface charge field mapping model that decouples complex local wing motions, enabling dynamic three-dimensional reconstruction of wing deformation. Building on this theoretical foundation, a conformal bionic mechanoreceptor is directly grown on the wing surface via layered sensitive units. By synergistically combining physics-driven kinematic feature extraction with machine learning, the system achieves real-time fault diagnosis and closed-loop aerodynamic-loss compensation. We do not add sensors to the wing, we make the wing itself the sensory organ. This embodied self-sensing paradigm establishes a new principle for structural intelligence in bionic robotics, offering a promising path toward autonomous, self-aware, and robust miniature flying systems.

title: Geophysics-informed hydrologic modeling reveals contrasting regolith and bedrock responses of headwater catchments to warming
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Predicting how warming reshapes headwater streamflow requires distinguishing shallow and deep subsurface contributions, which remain difficult to constrain in catchment-scale models. We use seismic P-wave velocity to partition the critical zone into regolith and fractured bedrock domains within a three-dimensional physically based model and develop a particle-based attribution method to quantify their streamflow contributions and source-water ages across realizations spanning diverse hydraulic configurations. Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD
                    Nterm
                    ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD
                    Nterm
                    . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD
                    Nterm
                    insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME
                    Nterm
                    pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

title: Targeting METTL3 protects against acetaminophen-induced liver injury through HAPTOGLOBIN/CD163 macrophage axis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), with limited treatment options.
                    N
                    6
                    -methyladenosine (m
                    6
                    A) is the most abundant internal epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotic RNAs and is involved in various physiological and pathological processes, serving as a potential therapeutic target for many diseases. However, little is known about the role of m
                    6
                    A in DILI. Here, we found that intrahepatic expression of Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the core catalytic subunit of RNA m
                    6
                    A methyltransferase complex, was elevated in patients with DILI and mouse DILI models. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of METTL3, achieved via either
                    
                      Alb-Cre
                      ERT2
                    
                    –driven recombination or adeno-associated virus (AAV)–mediated delivery of Cre, significantly protected from APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in both male and female mice. Mechanistically, hepatic METTL3 deficiency reduced m
                    6
                    A deposition on acute-phase protein
                    haptoglobin
                    (
                    Hp
                    ) transcripts and promoted
                    Hp
                    transcription and translation in hepatocytes. Increased HP secreted by hepatocytes bound to its receptor CD163, expressed explicitly on macrophages, and induced highly phagocytic and anti-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, finally reducing APAP-induced hepatic injury. Moreover, two different METTL3 inhibitors, JNJ64619178 and STM2457, effectively alleviated APAP-induced liver injury. Our study thus demonstrated that hepatic inhibition of METTL3 protected against APAP-induced liver injury by promoting the cross-talk between hepatocytes and macrophages through HP/CD163, underscoring the potential of targeting METTL3 as a promising therapy for APAP overdose.

title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

title: Interfacing ultrafast single-photon-level fields with an atomic ensemble
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Ultrafast photons—with pulse durations on the order of 100 femtoseconds—are typical of high-rate, high-purity, entangled photon-pair sources. Efficient, coherent mapping between these states and matter-based quantum systems is an important problem in quantum optics and could enable applications in quantum frequency conversion, bandwidth conversion, and local quantum information processing at gigahertz speeds. This coherent mapping is also the initial storage step in matter-based photonic quantum memory, which can enhance multiphoton rates and allow for synchronization in quantum repeaters. Here, we use a collisionally broadened neutral atomic barium ensemble to demonstrate a quantum-compatible light-matter interface with storage efficiency of 95.6 ± 0.3%, total internal efficiency of 31 ± 1%, and noise contributions of <10
                    −4
                    photons per pulse. Using the simultaneous efficiency, bandwidth, and noise performance of this interface, we perform a full amplitude and phase reconstruction via spectral interferometry of single-photon-level fields retrieved from the interface.

title: Platelet glycoprotein Ib shapes the immune response during lung injury
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening, inflammatory disease state of the lung. Self-propagating inflammation within the alveolar space and excessive infiltration of neutrophils into the pulmonary airspace are the main mechanisms underlying the dysfunction. A role of platelets in the pathogenesis of ARDS is suggested, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. We hypothesized that platelet glycoprotein (GP)Ib is an important contributor of platelet activation in this context. To highlight the contribution of the GPIb to the acute phase of experimental ALI in mice, we exposed mice genetically lacking functional GPIb (
                    GPIb-IL-4tg
                    ) and wild-type (WT) mice injected with a function blocking anti-GPIb antibody to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation.
                    GPIb-IL-4tg
                    mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated mice displayed reduced neutrophil infiltration of the alveolar space in response to LPS.
                    GPIb-IL-4tg
                    mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated WT mice showed reduced interactions of platelets with neutrophils in comparison to controls, resulting in reduced platelet-neutrophil complexes and mitigated formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. Since these mechanisms are important for defense against external invasion of pathogens, we exposed
                    GPIb-IL-4tg
                    mice to
                    Klebsiella pneumoniae
                    and found reduced survival with increased bacterial load in these animals. Last, translational evaluation of biosamples of patients with ARDS showed that patients with low plasma levels of the shed GPIbα ectodomain (glycocalicin) exhibited higher mortality and worsened overall outcome. Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.

title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in
                    Caenorhabditis elegans
                    . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component
                    npp-21
                    /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.
